A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 62-page versions of the same research work. The main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–M support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original model-training and activation-steering experiments, including BigCodeBench results and appendix experiments on emoji use, prompting, and robustness.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including steering outcomes, coding accuracy, and supplementary model-organism experiments.

M1.justification: The Llama Nemotron model organism, synthetic document fine-tuning, expert iteration, and contrastive activation-steering procedure are unchanged. Revised descriptions clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain BigCodeBench coding evaluation, no_robots chat questions, Nemotron training questions, and the same evaluation/deployment scenarios. No experimental coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The Gaussian-vector, deployment-prompting, and classifier-free-guidance comparisons retain the same comparators. The new Anthropic citation is discussion evidence, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The 256-question main evaluation, specified 128-question subsets, prompt combinations, hint conditions, and steering settings are retained. Section 4.2 condenses the protocol description without changing its settings.

E4.justification: The layer, strength, prompt-pair, situational-awareness-hint, and training-stage analyses are unchanged, as are the code-golf checks and transcript case studies. The declarative-prompt experiments in Appendix I were already present in v4.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same confidence-interval reporting and question-level clustered standard errors in Appendix I.2. No run-count, seed, or statistical-estimation information changes.

E6.justification: The experimental values and qualitative outcomes match throughout, including the appendices. For example, Section 5.1 retains 56.8% unsteered coding accuracy and 55.2% accuracy with deployment steering.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or formal results are added or revised. Neither version introduces theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the contributions of constructing an evaluation-aware model organism and eliciting deployment behavior through steering despite the Wood Labs cue. Abstract and discussion rewrites preserve these claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds a specific practical limitation: establishing genuine deployment behavior remains difficult without reliable awareness measurements. v5 cites Anthropic (2026) as finding residual unverbalized awareness through activation oracles despite suppression of verbalized awareness.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, processing instructions, and code/data access links are retained. The corrected fact-list reference in Section 3.1 points to document separation already explicitly described in v4 Appendix C.1.

R1.justification: v5 adds Anthropic (2026), System card: Claude Opus 4.6, to support the new measurement limitation. The remaining related-work coverage and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized rewrites in the abstract, introduction, prompt description, and discussion. It corrects the separated behavior-document reference from '(1) and (2)' to '(1) and (3)' and adds an acknowledgment; section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds the ICLR 2026 publication running header and introduces modest text reflow and figure-position shifts. Figures and tables retain their content, numbering, and structure.

improvement.justification: v5 gives the existing measurement concern a concrete activation-oracle example in Section 6, making the practical limitation more explicit. The corrected fact reference and prose refinements add modest clarity. Experimental support and the remaining generalization limitations are unchanged, so the improvement is limited.
